_about: Pindar in English, translator per title. Ernest Myers, The Extant Odes (1874), clean Gutenberg. Dawson W. Turner's literal prose (Bohn, 1852) with Abraham Moore's metrical version appended, raw IA OCR (1872 reprint, the cleaner scan). Moore's Olympic and Pythian odes also exist as a c1903 Boston reprint; not taken, it duplicates the Bohn appendix. Also: F. A. Paley's prose (1868) and C. A. Wheelwright's verse (Valpy, 1830), raw IA OCR. Cary's Pindar (1833) is on lane C's cary shelf: cross-referenced, not fetched (a duplicate row added here on 2026-10-03 was withdrawn on review). The 1810 Suttaby edition (pindar-west-greene-pye-1810-v1/v2) is a three-hand set: West's odes and Dissertation with further odes by R. B. Greene and H. J. Pye; vol. I is mostly the Dissertation.

pindar-turner-moore: The Odes of Pindar, literally translated into English prose (Bohn; 1872 printing)
tr. Dawson W. Turner (prose) and Abraham Moore (verse)
pindar-west-1749: Odes of Pindar, with several other pieces in prose and verse, with a dissertation on the Olympick games (London, 1749)
pindar-laurent-prose-1824: The Odes of Pindar in English Prose, with West's Dissertation on the Olympic Games (Oxford: Munday and Slatter, 1824), 2 vols. in one scan
tr. Peter Edmund Laurent per the catalogue (not named on the title page)
pindar-paley-1868: The Odes of Pindar translated into English Prose, with brief explanatory notes and a preface (London: Williams and Norgate, 1868)
pindar-wheelwright-1830: Pindar, translated (London: A. J. Valpy for Colburn and Bentley, 1830)
pindar-west-greene-pye-1810-v1: Odes of Pindar, translated from the Greek, with notes and illustrations, vol. I (West's Dissertation on the Olympic Games) (London: Suttaby, Evance and Hutchings, 1810)
tr. Gilbert West, R. B. Greene and H. J. Pye
pindar-west-greene-pye-1810-v2: Odes of Pindar, translated from the Greek, with notes and illustrations, vol. II (the odes) (London: Suttaby, Evance and Hutchings, 1810)
tr. Gilbert West, R. B. Greene and H. J. Pye
